entry.title: Praia de Galapos, Arrabida
entry.summary: Praia de Galapos is a sheltered bay of pale sand and fine pebbles below the green Arrabida mountains south of Lisbon. The water is clear, calm and turquoise, and the bay is protected by the hills, which makes it one of the nicest swimming beaches near the capital.

entry.title: Praia de Melides, Alentejo
entry.summary: Praia de Melides is a wide, wild beach of pale sand on the Alentejo coast, with a freshwater lagoon behind the dunes and almost no development. The Atlantic is powerful and cool, and the beach feels remote even in summer.

entry.title: Praia dos Salgados, Albufeira
entry.summary: Praia dos Salgados is a long beach of golden sand in the central Algarve, beside a protected coastal lagoon known for its birdlife. The sea is open and often breezy, and the beach is much wider and quieter than the town beaches nearby.

entry.title: Lerici Beach, Liguria
entry.summary: Lerici is a colourful harbour town on the Gulf of La Spezia, known as the Gulf of Poets, with a small beach of sand and pebbles below a medieval castle. The water is calm and clear, and narrow streets and pastel houses climb the hill behind.

entry.title: Numana Beach, Marche
entry.summary: Numana is a small town on the Conero Riviera in Marche, with beaches of fine white pebbles and clear green-blue water below the wooded slopes of Monte Conero. The coast is one of the few rocky stretches on the Adriatic, and the beaches here are among the cleanest in Italy.

entry.title: Noli Beach, Liguria
entry.summary: Noli is a small medieval seaside town on the Ligurian Riviera, with a beach of sand and pebbles below the old walls and towers. The water is clear and calm, colourful fishing boats are pulled up on the sand, and the island of Bergeggi sits just offshore.

entry.title: Mazzaro Beach, Taormina
entry.summary: Mazzaro is a pebble bay on the Ionian coast of Sicily, below the hill town of Taormina and connected to it by a cable car. The water is deep blue and clear, and the bay looks out towards the coast and Mount Etna on a clear day.

entry.title: Scivu Beach, Sardinia
entry.summary: Scivu is a wild beach on the Costa Verde of south-west Sardinia, with tall golden dunes that reach down to a long sweep of sand. The sea is open to the Atlantic-style waves of the western coast, and the area has almost no development.

entry.title: Ile-Rousse Beach, Corsica
entry.summary: Ile-Rousse is a lively seaside town in the Balagne on the north coast of Corsica, with a long town beach of sand and fine gravel and a small red-rock islet linked to the shore by a causeway. The water is clear and the mountains of the Balagne frame the view.

entry.title: Sagone Beach, Corsica
entry.summary: Sagone is a long beach of pale sand at the head of the gulf of the same name on the west coast of Corsica, with a Genoese tower on the point and mountains behind. The water is shallow and the beach is wide, which suits families.

entry.title: Cargese Beach (Peru), Corsica
entry.summary: Peru is a small sandy bay below the village of Cargese on the west coast of Corsica, with clear water and green maquis hills around it. Cargese itself was founded by Greek settlers, and the village has both Catholic and Orthodox churches facing each other.

entry.title: Algajola Beach, Corsica
entry.summary: Algajola is a small walled town in the Balagne on the north-west coast of Corsica, with a Genoese citadel beside a long beach of pale sand. The water is clear and shallow, and the mountains of the interior rise behind the village.

entry.title: Torre del Mar Beach, Velez-Malaga
entry.summary: Torre del Mar is a long beach of dark grey sand on the eastern Costa del Sol, with a wide promenade, palm trees and the mountains of the Axarquia behind. It feels like a Spanish town beach rather than a resort strip.

entry.title: Playa de la Mata, Torrevieja
entry.summary: Playa de la Mata is a long, flat beach of fine sand in Torrevieja on the Costa Blanca, with shallow water and a promenade behind. A large pink salt lagoon sits just inland, and the beach is a favourite with families in summer.

entry.title: Playa de Somo, Cantabria
entry.summary: Playa de Somo is a long, wide beach of golden sand on the Cantabrian coast, facing the city of Santander across the bay. The Atlantic waves make it one of the best places for surf lessons in northern Spain, and the sand is wide at low tide.

entry.title: Voulisma Beach, Istro
entry.summary: Voulisma is a beach of soft pale sand near the village of Istro in the Mirabello Bay of eastern Crete. The water is shallow, clear and light turquoise, and the bay is sheltered from many winds, which makes it a good choice for families.

entry.title: Fakistra Beach, Pelion
entry.summary: Fakistra is a small pebble beach on the Aegean coast of Pelion, reached by a steep road down through chestnut and olive trees. The water is deep blue and clear, and green hills fall steeply into the sea on both sides.

entry.title: Kefalos Beach, Kos
entry.summary: Kefalos is a long, open bay of sand on the south-west coast of Kos, with the small islet of Kastri and its white chapel of Agios Nikolaos at the western end. The beach is much quieter than the resorts on the north coast of the island.

entry.title: Marathias Beach, Zakynthos
entry.summary: Marathias is a small bay near Keri on the south-west coast of Zakynthos, framed by white limestone rocks and shallow turquoise water. A narrow strip of sand and pebbles runs along the bay, and the sea is calm in settled weather.

entry.title: Agios Pavlos Beach, Rethymno
entry.summary: Agios Pavlos is a quiet bay on the south coast of Crete, with pale sand dunes, a small chapel and a rocky cape that shelters the water on one side. The beach is far from the big resorts, and the coast around it is wild and open.

entry.title: Valtos Beach, Parga
entry.summary: Valtos is a long beach of sand and fine pebbles just over the headland from the town of Parga on the Ionian coast of Epirus. The water is clear and fairly calm, and pine-covered hills and a Venetian castle rise behind the bay.

entry.title: La Capte Beach, Hyeres
entry.summary: La Capte is a long beach of fine sand on the Giens peninsula near Hyeres, with pine trees behind and calm, shallow water. The steady wind makes it a favourite spot for windsurfing and kitesurfing, and the water stays shallow for a long way out.

entry.title: Kerfissien Beach, Cleder
entry.summary: Kerfissien is a wide beach of pale sand in Cleder, on the north coast of Finistere, dotted with pink granite boulders and backed by dunes. The tides change the beach a lot, and at low tide a large flat shore opens up for walking.

entry.title: Plage des Blancs-Sablons, Le Conquet
entry.summary: Les Blancs-Sablons is a wide beach of pale sand near Le Conquet at the western tip of Brittany, with dunes behind and the open Atlantic in front. The waves suit surfers, and the water is cold, so most visitors come for walks, views and the big sky.

entry.title: Praia do Magoito, Sintra
entry.summary: Praia do Magoito is a small sandy cove between golden sandstone cliffs on the Sintra coast, west of Lisbon. The Atlantic waves are strong and the water is cool, and the dramatic cliffs make it a popular spot for walks and sunset views.

entry.title: Praia de Sao Torpes, Sines
entry.summary: Praia de Sao Torpes is a sandy beach on the Alentejo coast near Sines, sheltered by a long breakwater that keeps the water calmer than on neighbouring beaches. Dunes and low scrub run behind, and the water is clear.

entry.title: Praia da Mareta, Sagres
entry.summary: Praia da Mareta is a sandy beach below the ochre cliffs of Sagres in the western Algarve, close to the village centre. The beach is sheltered from some winds by the cliffs, and the water is cool and clear, with the Sagres fortress nearby.

entry.title: Omis Beach
entry.summary: Omis is a small Dalmatian town at the mouth of the Cetina river, wedged between steep limestone mountains and the sea. The town beach is made of pebbles with clear water, and the setting makes it one of the most dramatic on the Adriatic.

entry.title: Gradac Beach, Makarska Riviera
entry.summary: Gradac is a pebble beach town at the southern end of the Makarska Riviera, with a long promenade, clear water and the Biokovo mountains rising steeply behind. It is quieter than the resorts further north and has a relaxed, family feel.

entry.title: Soline Beach, Brela
entry.summary: Soline is a pebble beach beside the village of Brela on the Makarska Riviera, shaded by pines, with clear turquoise water and the Biokovo mountains behind. It sits next to the better-known Punta Rata beach and is a little quieter.
